topics.topic: Behavior when `required_headers` includes kernel-managed HTTP headers (`host`, `accept-encoding`, `content-type`, `content-length`): reject, override, or duplicate handling
questions: What must the kernel do if `required_headers` includes one of these fixed headers (`host`, `accept-encoding`, `content-type`, `content-length`) with a different value or casing-normalized duplicate name?
What happens if `required_headers` contains `host`, `accept-encoding`, `content-type`, or `content-length` (case-insensitive): refuse, override kernel values, or send duplicates?

judgement.divergence: Behavior A: if `required_headers` contains `host`, `accept-encoding`, `content-type`, or `content-length` (case-insensitive), the kernel refuses (as manifest mismatch or pre-send failure) and sends nothing. Behavior B: the kernel still sends, either overriding its fixed header values or emitting duplicate headers; the external service notices different on-wire headers, and the owner/agent notice different node outcomes and waiting/end states.
judgement.why: The rules fix both kernel-managed headers and required headers but do not choose collision handling between them, so different implementations can produce different observable send behavior.

topics.topic: Compose-and-prove behavior when a flow version references missing contract versions or bindings (reject vs keep unproven)
questions: If a composed flow version references a non-existent contract version or binding, must composition be refused as unknown reference (and keep nothing), or must the version be kept and marked unproven by proof phase 1?

topics.topic: Whether capture from failed execution is allowed after a run ends in non-`failed` states (`refused`/`cancelled`)
